es.summary: Una aplicación recibió permisos delegados o una asignación de app role sobre una API de Microsoft (Graph, Exchange, SharePoint o Azure AD) en Entra ID. Se debe confirmar si la concesión fue planificada y si los permisos son proporcionales.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de Azure AD Audit Logs cuyo properties.message es exactamente 'Add delegated permission grant' o 'Add app role assignment to service principal', es decir, concesiones de OAuth2 delegated permissions o de application permissions a un service principal.
es.why_it_matters: Un atacante puede obtener consentimiento (phishing de consentimiento, cuenta comprometida) para que una app acceda a correo, archivos o al directorio sin conocer contraseñas. Corresponde a ATT&CK T1528, robo de tokens de acceso de aplicación, y otorga persistencia que sobrevive a cambios de contraseña.
triage_steps: Revise properties.targetResources para identificar el service principal, su AppId y la API de recurso (Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online, SharePoint).
En modifiedProperties lea los scopes o el AppRole.Value concedidos; priorice Mail.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory o full_access_as_app.
Identifique al iniciador (properties.initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName o app) y si fue consentimiento de administrador (ConsentType AllPrincipals) o de un solo usuario.

Busque en +/- 15 minutos eventos 'Consent to application', 'Add service principal', 'Add OAuth2PermissionGrant' o nuevas credenciales ('Update application – Certificates and secrets management') para la misma app.
Revise los sign-in logs del usuario iniciador: IP de origen, ubicación, user agent, MFA y alertas de riesgo previas.
Valide el publisher de la app (verificado o no), los redirect URIs y si la app es nueva en el tenant o tiene nombre que imita servicios legítimos.
Consulte los service principal sign-ins y la actividad posterior de la app (lecturas masivas de buzones o archivos) en las horas siguientes.
false_positives: Despliegue legítimo de una aplicación aprobada que requiere esos permisos, con ticket de cambio asociado.
Administradores concediendo admin consent a herramientas corporativas (backup, MDM, CASB, conectores de SIEM).
Usuarios que consienten permisos de bajo riesgo (User.Read, openid, profile) a apps permitidas por la política de consentimiento.
response_steps: Confirme con el propietario de la app y el iniciador si la concesión estaba autorizada y documentada.
Si no está autorizada, elimine el permission grant o la app role assignment y deshabilite el service principal, conservando evidencia del audit log.
Si la cuenta iniciadora parece comprometida, revoque sus sesiones y refresh tokens, restablezca credenciales y revise sus métodos MFA.
Determine el alcance revisando los accesos de la app a buzones, SharePoint y el directorio durante el periodo expuesto.
Restrinja el consentimiento de usuarios y habilite el flujo de solicitud de admin consent para prevenir recurrencias.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel high es adecuado porque estas concesiones otorgan acceso persistente a datos sensibles de Microsoft 365 o al directorio, aunque muchas son legítimas y requieren validación.

en.summary: An application was granted delegated permissions or an app role assignment on a Microsoft API (Graph, Exchange, SharePoint or Azure AD) in Entra ID. Confirm the grant was planned and the permissions are proportionate.
en.what_it_detects: Azure AD Audit Log events whose properties.message equals 'Add delegated permission grant' or 'Add app role assignment to service principal', meaning OAuth2 delegated permissions or application permissions were granted to a service principal.
en.why_it_matters: Attackers use consent phishing or compromised accounts to let an app read mail, files or the directory without knowing passwords. This maps to ATT&CK T1528, stealing application access tokens, and gives persistence that survives password resets.
triage_steps: Check properties.targetResources for the service principal, its AppId and the resource API (Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online, SharePoint).
Read the granted scopes or AppRole.Value in modifiedProperties; prioritize Mail.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory or full_access_as_app.
Identify the initiator (properties.initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName or app) and whether it was admin consent (ConsentType AllPrincipals) or single-user consent.
Within +/- 15 minutes, look for 'Consent to application', 'Add service principal' or new credentials added to the same app.
Review the initiator's sign-in logs: source IP, location, user agent, MFA result and earlier risk alerts.
Validate the app publisher (verified or not), redirect URIs, whether the app is new to the tenant or mimics a legitimate service name.
Check service principal sign-ins and follow-on activity by the app, such as bulk mailbox or file reads, in the next hours.
false_positives: Legitimate rollout of an approved application that needs these permissions, backed by a change ticket.
Admins granting admin consent to corporate tools (backup, MDM, CASB, SIEM connectors).
Users consenting low-risk scopes (User.Read, openid, profile) to apps allowed by the consent policy.
response_steps: Confirm with the app owner and the initiator that the grant was authorized and documented.
If unauthorized, remove the permission grant or app role assignment and disable the service principal, preserving audit log evidence.
If the initiating account looks compromised, revoke its sessions and refresh tokens, reset credentials and review its MFA methods.
Scope impact by reviewing the app's access to mailboxes, SharePoint and the directory during the exposure window.
Restrict user consent and enable the admin consent request workflow to prevent recurrence.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because these grants give persistent access to sensitive Microsoft 365 data or the directory, though many are legitimate and need validation.
